business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Manipal operates a pan-India network of multispecialty hospitals delivering care from outpatient services to complex tertiary and quaternary interventions. As of September 30, 2025 it ran 38 hospitals (48 on a pro forma basis) with 10,761 licensed beds (12,367 pro forma) across 14 states and union territories. Clinical focus is on tertiary/quaternary care in cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopedics and renal sciences (CONGO-R).

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Manipal Hospitals Private Limited — Material Subsidiary: Borrowings to be repaid/prepaid from Fresh Issue Net Proceeds
- Sahyadri Hospitals Private Limited — Stepdown Subsidiary (acquired Oct 2025): Added 1,606 licensed beds; minority stake acquisition to be funded from Net Proceeds
- AMRI Hospital Private Limited — Acquired subsidiary (Sep 2023): Being integrated and upgraded
- Medica Synergie Private Limited — Acquired subsidiary (Jul 2024): Being integrated and upgraded
- Columbia Asia Hospitals Private Limited — Acquired subsidiary (Fiscal 2022): EBITDA margin improved from 27.41% to 31.95% between FY2023 and FY2025

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Clinical specialties (CONGO-R focus):** Cardiac sciences, Oncology, Neurosciences, Gastro sciences, Orthopedics, Renal sciences
- **Care levels:** Outpatient services, Tertiary care, Quaternary care

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Insurance / Third party administrators (~49.18% of revenue, FY2025 restated)
- Cash / self-pay (~31.20% of revenue, FY2025 restated)
- Government (~13.41% of revenue, FY2025 restated)
- Others (~6.21% of revenue, FY2025 restated)

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- NABH - National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (41 of 48 hospitals accredited/certified as of Sep 30, 2025)
- NABL - National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (25 hospital labs accredited)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Not a manufacturing supply chain. The DRHP describes an integrated, decentralized multi-hospital operating model (regional COOs, hospital directors and medical directors) and a vertically integrated clinical-talent pipeline: a DNB/DrNB/FNB ecosystem spanning 343 seats across 25 hospitals, 42 specialties and 659 students enrolled as of September 30, 2025 (pro forma), plus collaboration with Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) which supports doctor recruitment. Growth is driven by organic brownfield/greenfield expansion and strategic acquisitions (AMRI – September 2023, Medica Synergie – July 2024, Sahyadri – October 2025).

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body:
- Human Care Medical Charitable Trust (HCMCT) - O&M / management collaboration
- Eastern India Health Foundation (EIHF) - concession agreement
- Konkan Mitra Mandal Medical Trust (KMMMT) - MOU and management agreement

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Inpatient volume growth (0.28m in FY2023 to 0.44m in FY2025, 25.72% CAGR) driving revenue
- Rising CONGO-R high-acuity specialty mix supporting ARPOB and revenue quality
- Operational efficiency - ALOS held at 2.85-2.88 days (FY2023-FY2025), declining to 2.73 days in H1 FY2026
- Occupancy and operational-bed ramp of acquired/upgraded hospitals
- Post-acquisition margin improvement (e.g. Columbia Asia EBITDA margin 27.41% to 31.95%)
- Material cost to revenue held stable around ~20%

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand licensed bed capacity through greenfield projects and brownfield additions at existing hospitals
- Grow the high-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix while maintaining operational efficiency (stable/declining ALOS)
- Integrate and upgrade acquired hospital networks to lift utilisation and margins
- Deepen leadership in the three key regions (Karnataka; Maharashtra & Goa; eastern India) and metro markets
- Continue investing in advanced medical equipment, technology and clinical excellence

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Manipal plans to add approximately 751 licensed beds across existing hospitals and approximately 1,943 licensed beds through greenfield projects by 2030 to support growth. Its network grew from 28 hospitals with 7,699 licensed beds (Mar 31, 2023) to 48 hospitals with 12,367 licensed beds (pro forma, Sep 30, 2025), aided by acquisitions of AMRI (Sep 2023), Medica Synergie (Jul 2024) and Sahyadri (Oct 2025, adding 1,606 beds). In November 2025 it commenced its 49th hospital in Bengaluru, taking licensed capacity to 12,631 beds as of December 31, 2025.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest pan-India multispecialty hospital network by bed capacity and second largest by number of hospitals (Sep 30, 2025)
- Only private hospital chain leading in three metros - Bengaluru, Kolkata and Pune - by bed capacity
- Widest hospital footprint among private hospital chains in India across 14 states and union territories
- Balanced metro / non-metro presence (~42.72% beds in metros, ~57.28% in non-metros)
- High-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix (~60-64% of gross inpatient revenue) supporting revenue quality
- Highest revenue growth and among the highest EBITDA margin and ROCE among major hospital players (FY2023-FY2025, CRISIL)
- Track record of value-accretive acquisitions and post-acquisition margin improvement
- Backing of Promoters and global institutional investors (Temasek, TPG, Novo Holdings)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geographic concentration in Karnataka — Karnataka hospitals contributed 51.55% of FY2025 revenue (66.61% in FY2023); disruption or policy change there would materially hurt results
- Acquisition integration risk — Growth relies heavily on acquisitions (AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri); failure to integrate/upgrade could erode expected synergies
- Reliance on pro forma financials — Pro forma information reflecting the Acquisition Transactions may not be indicative of actual or future results
- O&M / managed-hospital agreement risk — Six O&M hospitals operated under trust agreements (HCMCT, EIHF, KMMMT) carry contractual continuation risk
- Payor mix dependence on insurance/TPA and government — ~49% of revenue from insurance/TPA and ~13% from government schemes exposes pricing to third-party and regulatory pressure
- Execution risk on bed-expansion plans — Planned ~751 brownfield and ~1,943 greenfield beds by 2030 depend on capex, approvals and ramp-up timelines
- Regulatory and accreditation dependence — Business depends on licensed-bed approvals and NABH/NABL accreditations that can be withdrawn or delayed

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Add approximately 751 licensed beds across existing hospitals by 2030.**
- **Add approximately 1,943 licensed beds through greenfield projects by 2030.**
- **Repay/prepay outstanding borrowings and accrued interest of Material Subsidiary Manipal Hospitals Private Limited from Fresh Issue Net Proceeds.**
- **Acquire minority stake in stepdown Subsidiary Sahyadri Hospitals Private Limited from Fresh Issue Net Proceeds.**
- **Raise gross proceeds of the Fresh Issue of Rs 80,000 million (with a possible Pre-IPO Placement of up to Rs 16,000 million).**
- **Continue growing the high-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix (cardiac, oncology, neuro, gastro, ortho, renal) while maintaining operational efficiency.**
- **Integrate and upgrade acquired networks (AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri) within the Manipal network.**
- **Ramp the 49th hospital in Bengaluru (commenced Nov 2025), which raised licensed bed capacity to 12,631 beds as of Dec 31, 2025.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand licensed bed capacity through greenfield projects and brownfield additions at existing hospitals
- Grow the high-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix while maintaining operational efficiency (stable/declining ALOS)
- Integrate and upgrade acquired hospital networks to lift utilisation and margins
- Deepen leadership in the three key regions (Karnataka; Maharashtra & Goa; eastern India) and metro markets
- Continue investing in advanced medical equipment, technology and clinical excellence
